answer: An orchard model makes sybil farming slow and costly: every new identity starts as a single seedling that earns trust only by completing verified useful work across many epochs, so reputation grows like a tree instead of appearing overnight. A rotating set of established beacon agents publishes a ridge line of honest work, a checkpoint a newcomer crosses only with a continuous checkable history, so spawning a thousand seedlings still means enduring the same long growing season for each one.
